keyVerseText: So it shall be a reproach and a taunt, an instruction and an astonishment unto the nations that are round about thee, when I shall execute judgments in thee in anger and in fury and in furious rebukes. I the LORD have spoken it.
rootMeaning: The root of גְּדוּפָה (gᵉdûwphâh) is גָּדַף (gâdaph), which fundamentally means to blaspheme or revile, especially through harsh or cutting speech. As a feminine passive participle, גְּדוּפָה carries the sense of something that has been subjected to such verbal abuse or reproach. This root meaning enriches the English translation 'taunt' by emphasizing not just mockery but a deep, cutting revilement that wounds through words.
usageInScripture: The word גְּדוּפָה appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Ezekiel 5:15, where it is translated as 'and a taunt.' This singular usage highlights its role as a severe form of reproach or public humiliation. The consistency of its translation as 'taunt' underscores its function as a scornful and pointed insult, reinforcing the gravity of the judgment described in the verse.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding גְּדוּפָה helps believers grasp the severity of divine judgment as not only punitive but also dishonoring in the eyes of surrounding nations. It reveals how God's justice can bring about a state where a people become objects of scorn and astonishment, emphasizing the holiness and righteousness of God in contrast to human sinfulness. This word reflects the biblical theme that sin leads to shame and reproach, but also points to the necessity of repentance and restoration through Christ, who bore ultimate reproach on behalf of sinners.
keyVerseReflection: Ezekiel 5:15 declares that the judgment upon the people will result in them becoming 'a reproach and a taunt, an instruction and an astonishment' to the nations nearby. The inclusion of גְּדוּפָה here intensifies the sense of disgrace and public humiliation that accompanies God's righteous anger. This word conveys that the judgment is not only punitive but also serves as a solemn warning and a vivid demonstration of God's justice to all observers.
